children: Kailash Babar & Maulik Vyas Mumbai: The Supreme Court upheld insolvency proceedings against Gstaad Hotels and Neo Capricorn Plaza, owners and operators of the JW Marriott hotel in Bengaluru and Crowne Plaza hotel in Pune, respectively, while clarifying that disputes over the precise quantum of outstanding debt cannot prevent the initiation of corporate insolvency resolution process.

Under the insolvency process, the Mumbai bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) last month approved Shree Naman Developers' combined 1,800 crore resolution plans for the two companies. The plan for Gstaad Hotels is valued at 1,611 crore, while that for Neo Capricorn Plaza is valued at 189 crore.

The combined resolution value exceeds the two companies' admitted liabilities of about 1,227 crore, a rare outcome in insolvency cases. The developer implemented the plan within the stipulated 30-day period and has acquired the properties. An apex court bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih dismissed appeals challenging orders of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) and the Mumbai bench of the NCLT, which had admitted insolvency petitions filed by Omkara Asset Reconstruction.

The October 15 judgment laid down that proceedings at the admission stage under Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code require a summary determination based on the preponderance of probabilities and documentary evidence, rather than a detailed reconciliation of every disputed accounting entry. The court distinguished between the occurrence of default, which it described as a historical event, and the quantum of outstanding debt, which can fluctuate due to interest, charges, adjustments and repayments.

Disputes over the amount owed do not negate a default if the statutory threshold for initiating insolvency proceedings is met, it said. The dispute arose from loans of 600 crore extended by Piramal Finance in December 2017 to the two hotel companies as co-borrowers. These included term loans and a revolving credit facility, alongside separate loans under the government's Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme.

The lenders assigned the facilities to Omkara Asset Reconstruction in December 2022. After recording defaults with National E-Governance Services, an information utility, Omkara recalled the outstanding facilities in February 2023 and subsequently filed insolvency petitions against both companies. The hotel operators challenged the proceedings, citing cash-management arrangements, debt-service reserve accounts, disputed interest calculations and the businesses' profitability.

title: SC Allows Insolvency of Gstaad Hotels, Neo Plaza
